claim: A cashless claim is one where the insurance company pays the hospital directly (O001: 'your cashless claim, where the insurance company pays the hospital directly, has just been denied')
source_quote: Cashless Facility means a facility extended by the insurer to the insured where the payments, of the costs of treatment undergone by the insured in accordance with the Policy terms and conditions, are directly made to the network provider by the insurer to the extent pre-authorization is approved.
note: Arogya Sanjeevani (IRDAI standard product) policy wording, Go Digit, UIN GODHLIP24179V022324, definition 7; fetched 2026-10-15, quote machine-checked. The plain-words gloss is fair: payment goes to a network hospital, up to the approved pre-authorisation. The 9 PM counter and the ₹4,50,000 bill are Episode 01's SIMULATION (E004-E005), labelled FROM EPISODE 1 · SIMULATION on screen.

claim: After a cashless denial you can still pay the hospital and claim the money back as reimbursement; the four-step plan (papers; reimbursement and the grievance officer; Bima Bharosa; the Ombudsman) is Episode 01's (O002, O003, O009, O029; on-screen at O002: STEP 4: INSURANCE OMBUDSMAN · FREE)
source_quote: the insured person may obtain the treatment as per treating doctor's advice and submit the claim documents to the Company/ TPA for reimbursement.
note: Go Digit Arogya Sanjeevani wording, procedure for cashless claims (vi), machine-checked; the same clause is in IFFCO-Tokio's wording (Episode 01, HC-01). The four steps are Episode 01's own advice (E044-E051), checked there (HC-16 to HC-19); steps 2 to 4 are re-checked here (IO-12 to IO-21).

claim: A claim that is partly cut is a 'partial repudiation' the Ombudsman can hear; example: ₹4,50,000 bill, ₹1,20,000 approved, ₹3,30,000 cut (O005; on-screen ₹4,50,000 BILL · ₹1,20,000 PAID · ₹3,30,000 CUT · EXAMPLE)
source_quote: (b) any partial or total repudiation of claims by the life insurer, General insurer or the health insurer;
note: Rule 13(1)(b), Insurance Ombudsman Rules 2017 as amended till 09.11.2023 (cioins.co.in PDF, byte-identical to the owner's S01 copy), machine-checked. The amounts are ours, labelled EXAMPLE; arithmetic checked: 4,50,000 - 1,20,000 = 3,30,000. v1.3 dropped 'silently' (insurers must explain a cut: health master circular para 17(b)).

claim: Consumer court cases often take a long time (O007: 'wait, often for a long time, for a verdict')
source_quote: More than one-third of filed cases in the 19 SCDRCs, which shared information, had been pending for more than three years.
note: India Justice Report, Consumer Justice Report 2026 press release (18 Mar 2026; RTI data from 19 State Commissions), machine-checked. The law asks commissions to decide within three months, or five with testing (Consumer Protection Act 2019 s.38(7), quoted in Lok Sabha unstarred question 886, 04.02.2026, https://fcainfoweb.nic.in/PMS/writereaddata/2026_LS_B_886.pdf). O006-O007 describe what families think. In law a consumer needs no lawyer and the District Commission fee is nil up to ₹5 lakh (National Consumer Helpline FAQ 39 'There is no need for an advocate or any other pleader' and FAQ 45 fee table, https://consumerhelpline.gov.in/public/knowledgebasedetails/Consumer%20Protection%20Act%202019); v1.3 dropped 'pay the fees' and says 'many families' (O006), so the line no longer implies either.

claim: Some private claim-recovery services ask for twenty percent or more of the money they recover as their fee, plus GST (O008: 'some ask for twenty percent or more'; O019, O020, O062)
source_quote: Upon successful resolution of your insurance complaint, we charge a success fee of 20% of the amount received (plus applicable GST). In cases resolved at the legal level, the success fee will be 22% of the amount received (plus applicable GST).
note: Insurance Samadhan FAQ, fetched 2026-10-15, machine-checked (plus a one-time registration fee of ₹999 after case acceptance). Others publish lower fees: GetClaims ₹5,000 acceptance fee plus 10-20% (https://getclaims.in/vs/insurance-samadhan), ClaimSarathee 10% (https://claimsarathee.in). 'Twenty percent or more' (v1.3) fits: 20% at company and Ombudsman level, 22% 'at the legal level'. No firm is named on screen (unbranded SIMULATION ad).

claim: Fee example: 20% of ₹3,30,000 = ₹66,000; plus 18% GST = ₹77,880 (O020-O021; on-screen ₹66,000 FEE + 18% GST = ₹77,880 · OUR CALCULATION, with the GST rate labelled as assumed)
source_quote: Heading 9983 (Other professional, technical and business services) (ii) Other professional, technical and business services other than [(i) and (ia) above and serial number 38 below 9 9 18
note: Required change 3 applied in v1.3: on-screen now reads ₹66,000 FEE + 18% GST (ASSUMED) = ₹77,880 · OUR CALCULATION. Arithmetic checked: 3,30,000 x 20% = 66,000; 66,000 x 18% = 11,880; 66,000 + 11,880 = 77,880. CBIC services rate table, Heading 9983 (ii): CGST 9 + SGST 9 = IGST 18, machine-checked. The firms quote only 'plus applicable GST', so 18% is our assumption about how the service is classified.

claim: Filing a complaint with the Ombudsman costs zero rupees (O010, O023, O024; on-screen FREE at O002, FREE TO FILE [CIO FAQ] at O010, FILING FEE: ₹0 [CIO FAQ] at O024; title 'Free')
source_quote: No charges are required to be paid for lodging a complaint with the Insurance Ombudsman.
note: CIO FAQ Q15 (live page, fetched 2026-10-15; same in the owner's S03 snapshot), machine-checked. IRDAI Policyholders' Interests master circular 2024, Part B VI.3(ii): 'without any charge / fee'. The [CIO FAQ] tag is right.

claim: When the Ombudsman passes an award it is binding on the insurance company (O010, O018, O056; on-screen AWARD BINDS THE INSURER [RULE 17] at O010, [RULE 17 | INSURANCE OMBUDSMAN RULES] at O056)
source_quote: (8) The award of Insurance Ombudsman shall be binding on the insurers
note: Rule 17(8), machine-checked; Rule 17(1): 'Where the complaint is not settled by way of mediation under rule 16, the Ombudsman shall pass an award'. Binding on the insurer only (IO-31). Insurers can still challenge an award by writ in a High Court (Bombay HC, Aditya Birla Sun Life v Insurance Ombudsman, 2022, cited by the Karnataka HC in 2026:KHC:32548-DB), which is why the penalty lines need the appeal exception (IO-10). v1.3 split the O010 tags, so 'binds' now carries [RULE 17].

claim: The insurer must carry out an award within thirty days of receiving it; if it does not honour the award it must pay the complainant ₹5,000 for every day of delay, on top of penal interest (O010, O012, O058, O059; on-screen ₹5,000 / DAY LATE [IRDAI HEALTH MASTER CIRCULAR | 2024] at O010, 30 DAYS FROM RECEIPT [IRDAI HEALTH MASTER CIRCULAR | 2024] at O058, ₹5,000 / DAY · NOT IF CHALLENGED IN 30 DAYS [IRDAI HEALTH FAQ 45 · POLICYHOLDERS' INTERESTS MASTER CIRCULAR | 2024] at O059)
source_quote: The Insurer is required to comply with the award of the Insurance Ombudsman within 30 days of receipt of award by the Insurer. In case the Insurer does not honour the ombudsman award, a penalty of Rs. 5000/- per day shall be payable to the complainant. Such penalty is in addition to the penal interest liable to be paid by the Insurer under The Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017.
note: Master Circular on Health Insurance Business, IRDAI/HLT/CIR/PRO/84/5/2024, 29.05.2024, para 20 'Implementation of Ombudsman Award' (English PDF on this page, re-downloaded 2026-10-15), machine-checked. The same words are IRDAI health FAQ Q45 (https://irdai.gov.in/health-dept, page updated 09 Oct 2026), and Rule 17(6) gives the 30 days ('shall comply with the award within thirty days of the receipt of the award'). Both tags are right. The penalty has an exception: IO-10.

claim: The ₹5,000-a-day penalty applies only if the company has not challenged (appealed) the award within the thirty days (O010: 'if the company does not challenge the award, but pays it late'; O059: 'and it has not challenged the award within those thirty days'; on-screen NOT IF CHALLENGED IN 30 DAYS)
source_quote: ii. In case the Insurer does not honour the Insurance Ombudsman award within 30 days, a penalty of Rs. 5000/- per day shall be payable to the complainant for each day of delay. iii. Such penalty is in addition to the penal interest liable to be paid by the Insurer under the Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017. iv. This provision will not be applicable in case insurer chooses to appeal against the award of the Insurance Ombudsman within 30days. In such case, due intimation shall be sent to the Policyholder.
note: Required changes 1 and 7 applied in v1.3 (word for word). Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests 2024, IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024, 5 Sep 2024, Part B (health insurance) VI.4 'Implementation of Ombudsman Award', machine-checked; paras 25.3-25.4 say the same. It is later than the 29 May 2024 health circular, so the exception applies to health awards. There is no statutory appeal: insurers challenge awards by writ petition. Episode 01 made the same fix (HC-29b).

claim: Skipping the first step gets complaints turned away: 'In twenty twenty-four to twenty-five alone, seventeen hundred and fifteen health complaints were turned away for this one reason. The person had not complained to the insurance company first.' (O027; O012 'one common mistake'; O025, O026; on-screen 1,715 HEALTH COMPLAINTS TURNED AWAY · NO COMPLAINT TO THE INSURER FIRST [CIO ANNUAL REPORT 2024–25 | STATEMENT H8])
source_quote: NATURE WISE CLASSIFICATION OF COMPLAINTS RECEIVED FOR THE PERIOD FROM 01.04.2024 to 31.03.2025 STATEMENT H 8 HEALTH INSURANCE ... Total 1030 1781 1715 38 364 4928 239 26507 244 77 9 404 34 28 33 27575 32503 ... Customer Not represented to Ins. Co. [14(3)(a)]
note: CIO Annual Report 2024-25, Statement H8 (printed p.63, PDF p.72; scanned, read from the page image, saved as sources/cio-2024-25-H8-health-nature-wise-pdfp72.jpg; column sums checked). Non-entertainable health complaints: beyond the Rules 1,030; not within jurisdiction [14(1)] 1,781; no complaint to the insurer first [14(3)(a)] 1,715; sub judice [14(5)] 38; over one year [14(3)(b)] 364; total 4,928 of 32,503 received. Annual Report 2023-24, Statement H8 (text PDF, https://cioins.co.in/annualreports/AnnualReport2023-2024.pdf): 3,869 of 6,699 non-entertainable health complaints were 14(3)(a). v1.3 uses the 1,715 at O027 with the H8 tag: 'turned away' = classified non-entertainable, 'this one reason' = Rule 14(3)(a). In 2024-25 the wrong-office reason (1,781) was slightly larger, so v1.3's 'one common mistake' (O012) is the right wording.

claim: Bima Bharosa is the insurance regulator's (IRDAI's) online complaint portal; a complaint registered there goes to the insurance company and onto IRDAI's records (O002, O014, O015, O017; on-screen bimabharosa.irdai.gov.in)
source_quote: A complaint registered through Bima Bharosa will flow to the insurance company's system as well as the IRDAI repository. Thus, Bima Bharosa provides a standard platform to all insurance companies to resolve proposer or policyholder's grievances and provides IRDAI with a tool to monitor the effectiveness of the grievance redress system of insurance companies.
note: IRDAI Grievance Cell FAQ page (updated 09 Oct 2026), 'What is Integrated Grievance Management System?', machine-checked (the page uses curly apostrophes). Same page: 'Bima Bharosa provides a gateway to register complaints with insurance companies and track their status.' PIB, Ministry of Finance, 14 Aug 2026 (Release ID 2299382): 'The Complaints Management Systems of insurers and the Bima Bharosa Portal are integrated.' The URL on screen is right.

claim: Bima Bharosa 'often works. But if it does not work for you, do not stop there.' (O014; on-screen 63% SETTLED FOR THE POLICYHOLDER, 2025–26 [IRDAI CONSULTATION PAPER | 2026]); many still get a rejection and the complaint is closed (O015)
source_quote: In FY26, 63% of complaints disposed of in Bima Bharosa were settled in favour of policyholders. Policyholders not satisfied with the decision at this level have the option to approach the Ombudsman. Out of the claims disposed at the Ombudsman's level a further 75% were settled in favour of the customer.
note: Required change 2 applied in v1.3 (the unsourced 'Many families stop there ... not enough' is gone). IRDAI Consultation Paper on Distribution Reforms, Part 1 (23 Sep 2026), para 58; the IRDAI PDF on this page was machine-checked (byte-identical to the copy Value Research quoted on 10 Oct 2026). The 63% covers all lines of insurance, not health alone. O015 stays true: 37% of FY26 Bima Bharosa disposals did not go the policyholder's way, and the insurer closes a complaint if the complainant 'does not come back within 8 weeks' (IRDAI Grievance Cell FAQ).

claim: Bima Bharosa is useful but not a court: the company has to answer, IRDAI tracks it, the resolution comes from the insurance company, and Bima Bharosa 'does not decide your claim, and it does not pass an order telling the company to pay you' (O016, O017; on-screen TRACKS · DOES NOT DECIDE [BIMA BHAROSA | IRDAI])
source_quote: The documents relating to the complaint are captured and forwarded to the insurance company for resolution. The insurance company is required to examine the complaint and attend to it within two weeks by responding to the complainant. ... IRDAI will take it up with the insurance company concerned and shall facilitate re-examination of the complaint and resolution by the insurance company. ... In case the complainant is not satisfied with the resolution of the insurance company, he may approach the Insurance Ombudsman or the appropriate legal authority.
note: IRDAI Grievance Cell FAQ ('How are grievances handled at IRDAI?' and 'What is the course of action...'), machine-checked. No IRDAI page describes IRDAI or Bima Bharosa deciding a claim or ordering payment: the insurer resolves, IRDAI facilitates and monitors. v1.3 says 'does not pass an order' (was 'cannot'), which matches these pages. O016 'government portal' is the viewer's thought; it is the statutory regulator's portal on a gov.in address.

claim: The Insurance Ombudsman 'works under the Insurance Ombudsman Rules, twenty seventeen' (O018; on-screen [INSURANCE OMBUDSMAN RULES | 2017])
source_quote: In exercise of the powers conferred by section 24 of the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 1999 (41 of 1999) and in supersession of the Redressal of Public Grievances Rules, 1998, except as respects things done or omitted to be done before such supersession, the Central Government hereby makes the following rules
note: Preamble of the 2017 Rules, machine-checked. The institution dates from 1998-99 (CIO FAQ: 'established and is functioning since 1999'); today's Ombudsmen are appointed under Rule 7 of the 2017 Rules (Rule 4(1)(e)), v1.3's 'which works under' is exact. No amendment since 9 Nov 2023: cioins.co.in/OmbudsmanRules2017 lists the Rules 'as amended till 09.11.2023', and the Draft Amendment Rules 2025 (G.S.R. 864(E), 25 Nov 2025) were still not notified at the end of September 2026 (iPleaders, https://blog.ipleaders.in/insurance-ombudsman-complaint-procedure-and-awards/).

claim: Under Rule 14 the complaint is made by the person with the grievance, or through the legal heir, nominee or assignee (O022; on-screen [RULE 14 | INSURANCE OMBUDSMAN RULES])
source_quote: (1) Any person who has a grievance against an insurer [or insurance broker] may himself or through his legal heirs, nominee or assignee, make a complaint in writing to the Insurance Ombudsman
note: Rule 14(1), machine-checked (footnote markers dropped). The paraphrase is exact. It does not by itself make paid-help contracts void; the owner's Section 23 Contract Act line stays out, as the asset pack advised.

claim: File online on the official website cioins.co.in: choose Register Complaint and verify your mobile number with an OTP (O039, O040; on-screen cioins.co.in)
source_quote: Complaint can be registered online by clicking on the "Register complaint" under the Section "Complaint Online" on the webpage.
note: CIO FAQ Q6 (live), machine-checked. Complaint form (https://cioins.co.in/Complaint, fetched 2026-10-15): 'Enter your mobile number' ... 'You will receive an OTP on your registered mobile. The OTP is valid for 90 seconds.' Rule 14(2) allows complaints 'online through the website of the Council for Insurance Ombudsmen'.

claim: Two-step clock: first complain in writing to the insurance company, best of all its Grievance Redressal Officer; the Ombudsman door opens when the company rejects it, you are not happy with its reply, or one month passes with no reply (O025, O028, O029, O031, O033, O034; on-screen 1 MONTH [RULE 14(3)])
source_quote: (3) No complaint to the Insurance Ombudsman shall lie unless (a) the complainant [has made a representation in writing or through electronic mail or online through website of the insurer or insurance broker concerned] named in the complaint and- (i) either the insurer [or insurance broker, as the case may be,] had rejected the complaint; or (ii) the complainant had not received any reply within a period of one month after the insurer [or insurance broker, as the case may be,] received his representation; or (iii) the complainant is not satisfied with the reply given to him by the insurer
note: Rule 14(3)(a), machine-checked. The GRO: PIB, 14 Aug 2026 (Release ID 2299382): 'The Grievance Redressal Officer (GRO) of the insurer is the nodal officer for dealing with grievances.' The [RULE 14(3)] tag at O033 is right.

claim: 'Every insurer has to show its grievance officer's details on its website, and the Ombudsman's website lists their email addresses too.' (O030)
source_quote: (ix) Ensure that there is a Grievance Redressal officer in place who shall be responsible for grievance redressal and whose details are shall be made available at the website
note: IRDAI Master Circular on Corporate Governance for Insurers 2024 (IRDAI/F&I/CIR/MISC/82/5/2024, 22.05.2024), duties of the PPGR&CM Committee (ix); English PDF on this page, machine-checked. The rule says 'details'; the Ombudsman's own site lists every insurer's 'GRO Email Id' (https://cioins.co.in/GRONonLife, https://cioins.co.in/GROLife), which supports the second half of the v1.3 line.

claim: Under IRDAI rules the company should resolve your grievance within fourteen days (O002, O032; on-screen 14 DAYS [IRDAI POLICYHOLDERS' INTERESTS MASTER CIRCULAR | 2024])
source_quote: On receipt of a complaint, the complainant will have to be given an acknowledgement immediately. Insurers should provide resolution to the complaint within 14 days along with the reasons for not accepting the complaint with specific reference to the relevant terms and conditions of the policy.
note: Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests 2024 (5 Sep 2024), Part B (health) VI.2(i), machine-checked. Same 14 days: IRDAI health FAQ Q40, PIB 14 Aug 2026, Bima Bharosa home page ('Your complaint will be attended to within 14 days'); older IRDAI pages still say two weeks or 15 days. The tag is right. The 14 days is separate from the one-month wait in Rule 14(3), as the script keeps it.

claim: From the day the door opens you have one year to file, for compensation of up to fifty lakh rupees (O035; on-screen 1 YEAR · UP TO ₹50 LAKH [CIO FAQ])
source_quote: The complaint is being made to the Insurance Ombudsman within one year from: (a) Date of rejection of the complaint by the Insurance Company/Insurance Broker (b) Expiry of one month of filing the complaint if the Insurer/Broker fails to reply • The amount of Compensation sought in Insurance Ombudsman should not exceed Rs. 50 Lakhs.
note: CIO FAQ Q11 (live), machine-checked. Rule 14(3)(b): one year from the rejection, the unsatisfactory reply, or one month after sending the representation. Rule 17(3) proviso (ii): 'not award compensation exceeding rupees fifty lakhs (including relevant expenses, if any)'. Rule 14(4) lets the Ombudsman condone a delay (optional mention). The tag is right.

claim: The limit was raised from thirty to fifty lakh rupees in November 2023 by G.S.R. 828(E) (O036; on-screen [GAZETTE G.S.R. 828(E) | 2023])
source_quote: New Delhi, the 9th November, 2023 G.S.R. 828(E).-In exercise of the powers conferred by section 24 of the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 1999 (41 of 1999), the Central Government hereby makes the following rules further to amend the Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017 ... in sub-rule (3), in the proviso, in clause (ii), for the word 'thirty', the word 'fifty' shall be substituted.
note: Insurance Ombudsman (Amendment) Rules 2023, Ministry of Finance (DFS), para 6(ii); in force on publication in the Gazette. The PDF's text layer is OCR ('substiflrted'), so the last word was read from the page. The consolidated Rules carry the footnote 'Substituted by notification G.S.R. 828 (E), dated 9.11.2023'. The tag is right.

claim: The Ombudsman cannot take your complaint if the same dispute is already pending, or already decided, in any court, consumer forum, or arbitration (O037; on-screen PENDING OR DECIDED ELSEWHERE = NOT ALLOWED [RULE 14(5)])
source_quote: (5) No complaint before the Insurance Ombudsman shall be maintainable on the same subject matter on which proceedings are pending before or disposed of by any court or consumer forum or arbitrator.
note: Required change 4 applied in v1.3: the tag now reads [RULE 14(5)] (was 14(3)); machine-checked. The VO is right. 'Already decided' is a fair gloss of 'disposed of'; 'already closed' also covers a case withdrawn or dismissed (optional). CIO FAQ Q10 repeats the rule. The owner's audit puts it in 'Rule 14(3)(c)-(d)', which do not exist in the current text.

claim: There are eighteen Ombudsman offices, in cities like Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Mumbai, Delhi and Kolkata; you choose the office that covers where you live or the insurance company's branch or office (O041; on-screen 18 OMBUDSMAN OFFICES [CIO OFFICE DIRECTORY])
source_quote: AHMEDABAD BENGALURU BHOPAL BHUBANESWAR CHANDIGARH CHENNAI DELHI GUWAHATI HYDERABAD JAIPUR KOCHI KOLKATA LUCKNOW MUMBAI NOIDA PATNA PUNE THANE
note: CIO directory (live, 2026-10-15), 18 centres, machine-checked. Annual Report 2024-25 preface (PDF p.7, image in sources/): 'This year 2024-25 witnessed the opening of the 18th Office of Insurance Ombudsman at Thane ... The office commenced operations from 27.12.2024'. The CIO FAQ still says '17 offices' (out of date). Choice: complaint form 'Please choose the centre if your residential address or place of residence or branch / office of the Insurance Company falls under the jurisdiction.'; Rule 14(1) says the branch or office 'complained against', so 'the insurance company's branch or office you are complaining against' is more exact than 'that handled your policy' (optional). 1,781 health complaints in 2024-25 were classified 'Not within Jurisdiction [14(1)]' (IO-11).

claim: Documents: policy copy, discharge summary and final bill, rejection or deduction letter, your complaint to the insurer, ID and address proof, a photograph; each file a PDF or JPG up to 10 MB (O042-O047; on-screen PDF / JPG · MAX 10 MB EACH [CIOINS.CO.IN])
source_quote: You are requested to upload the following documents. Kindly note that each document size must not exceed 10 MB. Supported file types are *.pdf and *.jpg Copy of complaint submitted to Insurance Company * Valid ID Proof and Address Proof* Letter from Insurance Company rejecting the complaint/repudiating the claim Photograph Copy of Insurance policy Other document(s)
note: Live complaint form (fetched 2026-10-15), machine-checked. Only the copy of the complaint to the insurer and the ID/address proof are marked mandatory (*). CIO FAQ Q7 adds 'Photograph (in case of online registration of complaints)'. The discharge summary and bill go under 'Other document(s)' (Rule 14(2): facts 'supported by documents'). The tag is right.

claim: Tick the declaration and submit; the complaint is verified first and then registered; save the acknowledgement and complaint number (O048)
source_quote: I hereby declare that the information given by me is correct to the best of my knowledge. ... Thank you for submitting your complaint. Complaint details would be verified by us and post successful verification, your complaint would be registered.
note: Live complaint form, machine-checked; the confirmation screen shows the 'Complaint Number' and a 'View/Download Complaint' button. The owner's emailed 'Annexure VI-A' step is not on the current form and stays out.

claim: 'The Ombudsman hears both sides, you and the company. The hearing can be in person, or online by video.' (O050; on-screen ILLUSTRATIVE HEARING); 'If there is no settlement, the Ombudsman decides the case, and passes an award.' (O052)
source_quote: Wherever considered necessary, the Insurance Ombudsman will conduct hearing of both the parties either in person or through video conferencing.
note: Required change 5 applied in v1.3 (hearing first at O050, mediation at O051, award at O052; the unsourced v1.2 O051 'Often ... the company agrees to pay before any hearing takes place' is gone). It had no source, and the CIO's own figures point the other way: every centre's brief review in the Annual Report 2024-25 (printed pp.71-79) shows 100% of entertainable complaints 'disposed through online hearing' or 'off line hearing', with mediation as a share of them (Ahmedabad: 3,415 online, 355 offline; 'Centre has disposed off 35.70 % of entertainable complaints through recommendation (Mediation)'; image in sources/). So v1.2's O052 ('If there is no settlement, there is a hearing') had the order wrong: the hearing comes first, and settlements are reached through it. Rule 15(4): 'The Ombudsman shall dispose of a complaint after giving the parties to the dispute a reasonable opportunity of being heard.' Rule 15(5): video-conference. Rule 17(1): award where not settled by mediation. Preface: 'Online hearings also increased to 76%' (all lines, 2024-25). CIO FAQ Q16 machine-checked.

claim: 'Many complaints end in mediation under Rule sixteen. The Ombudsman suggests a fair settlement, and if both sides agree, the case closes.' (O051)
source_quote: Where a complaint is settled through mediation, the Ombudsman shall make a recommendation which it thinks fair in the circumstances of the case, within one month of the date of receipt of mutual written consent for such mediation
note: Rule 16(1), machine-checked; Rule 16(2): the complainant accepts in writing within fifteen days 'as full and final'; Rule 16(3): the insurer complies within fifteen days. 'If both sides agree' matches the mutual written consent and acceptance.

claim: 'In twenty twenty-four to twenty-five, about one in three health complaints that were closed, ended this way' (mediation; 9,417 of 29,017) (O051; on-screen ≈ 1 IN 3 · OUR CALCULATION [CIO ANNUAL REPORT | 2024–25])
source_quote: Complaints Disposal Statement for the period 01.04.2024 to 31.03.2025 STATEMENT H3 HEALTH INSURANCE ... Total 4928 32503 37431 9417 6126 4897 3649 4928 29017 22791 4343 1883 29017 3588 4423 403 8414
note: Required change 5 applied in v1.3: 'Last year' became 'In twenty twenty-four to twenty-five'. 2024-25 is the latest CIO report (cioins.co.in/AnnualReports, checked 2026-10-15); in a late-2026 film 'last year' means 2025. Statement H3, PDF pp.55-56 (scanned; read from the page images, saved in sources/; same figures as Episode 01 HC-25): 9,417 recommendations / 29,017 disposed = 32.5%, about one in three (our calculation). Recommendations are mediated settlements the complainant accepted (Rule 16(2)); the CIO counts them 'in favour of complainants' (Statement H5) and as 'redressed by way of recommendation (mediation)' (Annual Report 2023-24). The owner's 'over forty percent' would need another base (9,417 of 20,440 settled or decided = 46%). The CIO's centre-wise table H2 (PDF p.49, image in sources/) differs slightly from the company-wise H3: 32,655 received, 9,418 recommendations, 29,156 disposed, so 9,418 / 29,156 = 32.3%, the same 'about one in three'. The owner's audit quotes H2.

claim: You don't need a lawyer or legal words before the Ombudsman (O053; title 'No Lawyer Fees')
source_quote: Do I need to approach the Insurance Ombudsman through a lawyer? Our Response : As per the Insurance Ombudsman Rules 2017, there is no provision to engage a lawyer.
note: CIO FAQ Q12 (live), machine-checked. New since June 2026: the Karnataka High Court (Division Bench, 1 July 2026, WA 1534/2026, 2026:KHC:32548-DB) upheld an order letting a complainant bring an advocate once the case reaches the Rule 17 award stage (no lawyers at the mediation stage), following the Telangana High Court (N. Vijaya Laxmi v IRDAI, 2023). A lawyer is optional at the award stage in those states and never required, so O053 and 'No Lawyer Fees' stay true (IO-37).

claim: If you are not happy with the award you don't have to accept it; other remedies such as the consumer forum may still be open (O057)
source_quote: The award of Insurance Ombudsman shall be binding on the insurers (or insurance broker, as the case may be). However, if the complainant is not satisfied with the decision of the Insurance Ombudsman, he/she may exercise the right to take recourse to the normal process of law against the Insurance Company/Insurance Broker.
note: CIO FAQ Q21 (live), machine-checked. Rule 17 has no acceptance step for the complainant (unlike Rule 16(2) for mediated settlements) and Rule 17(8) binds only the insurer. 'May still be open' is the right hedge (time limits and the Rule 14(5) bar run the other way).

claim: Penal interest is due on top of the penalty: 2% above the bank rate from the date the claim ought to have been settled (O059 'on top of any interest that is due')
source_quote: 25.2. The insurer, in terms of rule 17 (7) of Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017, shall also pay penal interest at a rate, which is 2 percent above bank rate from the date the claim ought to have been settled.
note: Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests 2024, Chapter VII para 25.2, machine-checked. Rule 17(7) itself only says 'such interest at a rate per annum as specified in the regulations ... from the date the claim ought to have been settled under the regulations, till the date of payment'. Part B V.2(ii): a late health claim earns 'interest at bank rate plus 2 percent from the date of receipt of intimation to till the date of payment'. So the owner's 'Bank Rate plus two percent' is real (an IRDAI circular, not printed in Rule 17); the script's 'any interest that is due' is safe.
